messages:
maria_support: @josh_customer flagging this thread — customer reports sudden latency spike and we see region mismatch in headers.
josh_customer: Seeing 900-1300ms on /v1/generate over the last 20m. Account is pinned to us-west-2 but responses have x-served-region: eu-west-1.
maria_support: Oof. Can you paste raw response headers and a sample request trace id? Also did this start after any config change?
josh_customer: Headers: `x-redwood-region: us-west-2`, `x-served-region: eu-west-1`, `x-request-id: r-9f3b2`. No config changes on our side.
sam_sre: Thanks. Attaching quick checklist: 1) trace ID, 2) full request+response headers, 3) last 3 request timestamps. If it's routing, likely smart-routing fallback or stale routing table.
josh_customer: Trace attached inline: `trace: r-9f3b2, span sequence router->edge->inference, durations: router 12ms, edge 18ms, inference 820ms` — big jump due to cross-region hop.
efekaterina?: (note: typo) -- sorry, meant ekaterina_runtime.
ekaterina_runtime: Looking at r-9f3b2 on the router — router selected eu-west-1 because the customer's region tag was not found in the latest cache and the fallback policy prefers lowest-cost region when affinity unknown.
maria_support: Where did affinity go missing? customer is pinned in account metadata.
ekaterina_runtime: Our cache eviction window expired for that account after a hot restart on router pool in us-west-2. The router re-evaluated policy and picked eu-west-1 as fallback. Edge should have honored `x-region-pin` header but we see it was not sent from the client's SDK.
josh_customer: We didn't change SDK. How can we reproduce? We can try to force header.
sam_sre: To reproduce from customer side: curl with: 
```
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -H "x-region-pin: us-west-2" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Check `x-served-region` and `x-router-cache-hit` in response.
josh_customer: Ran the curl test — when I omit x-region-pin, server responds from eu-west-1. When I add x-region-pin, it still sometimes goes to eu-west-1 (~1/5 requests). Response headers show `x-router-cache-hit: false` on failures.
emekaterina_runtime: That aligns with a race where router pool is rebuilding and some nodes haven't loaded the pin store. We're rolling a fix: ensure router consults central pinstore before falling back. For immediate mitigation, set account-level hard pin in the account service; that bypasses cache for 24h.
maria_support: Communicated mitigation to customer: set hard pin or enable sticky-session on their side. Also we've opened an internal incident to fix router startup ordering.
sam_sre: Filed INC-2026-0732 to track. I'll add traces and heatmap for the last 6h to show percent of requests routed cross-region.
tracebot: Collected trace summary for r-9f3b2 and 842 other traces: 4.6% of requests for this account had `x-served-region` != `x-redwood-region` in the 2h window; spike correlates with router pool restart at 1718001200.
josh_customer: Thanks — applying hard pin now and will monitor. Appreciate quick triage :heart:
maria_support: We'll follow up when router fix is deployed. Closing loop after the deploy and postmortem.
